summary: Wooden light on the Thumb of Grand Island, Munising, lit 1868 and last lit 1908; a privately owned, closed house restored in 2002-2005.

structures.note: Square wooden tower joined to the gable end of the keeper's dwelling (LighthouseFriends). The archive gives 1870 as the tower's year; LighthouseFriends says it was first exhibited in 1868.
One-and-a-half-story keeper's dwelling on a stone foundation (LighthouseFriends); the archive gives the quarters as 1870. Lifted off the foundation and rebuilt in part in 2002-2005.

access.note: Privately owned; on private land and cannot be reached by land. Grounds, dwelling and tower closed. Seen from tour boats out of Munising.

facts.agency: Private owners (shares held since the 1913 sale to Munising Moose Lodge members; LighthouseFriends)

wrecks.outcome: Took shelter in Grand Island Harbor on 24 October 1903; grounded on a reef beside the light the next day after her steering chain broke; fire burned her to the waterline. LighthouseFriends only.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends says the light was first exhibited on 15 August 1868; the archive gives 1870 as the year the tower and quarters were established; the Forest Service says the Board spent its money on the light and the range lights in 1868-70. The story treats 1868 as the first light and 1870 as the archive's date for the tower and quarters.

LighthouseFriends says the light was last lit on 29 October 1908; the archive and the Forest Service date the end of the station to 1913. The 1913 date matches the sale of the reservation (LighthouseFriends), so the story gives 1908 for the light going dark and 1913 as the archive's discontinuance.

notes_for_editor: NRHP 80004835 (listed in the record) could not be read: the NPS file at the nomination address is a 1.9 KB placeholder image, so the story does not rely on the nomination. Conflicts left in the story: lightning date 5 August 1891 (Board report, fiscal 1892) vs 15 August 1891 (LighthouseFriends); the 1860 and 1866 appropriations (LighthouseFriends: $6,000 in 1860 and $10,000 in 1866) vs June 1864 and June 1866 (Forest Service, without sums); first exhibition 1868 vs archive 1870; last light 1908 vs archive/Forest Service 1913. Single-source items: the 1903 Manhattan wreck, the 1898 erosion and move plan, the 1905-1907 range-light requests and Congress's $15,000 (LighthouseFriends; the Board reports for 1898, 1902-1907 are not in the corpus), Prior's rescue of nine (undated), the 1863 committee and the 1860 petition (as quoted by LighthouseFriends; not read in the original), the 1999-2005 restoration (LighthouseFriends only). Keepers: six principal keepers from the archive roster, no assistants. Theresa Prior and the Prior children are family, not keepers; the sources give no role for her. No women keepers appear in the archive roster. The Munising Visitor's Bureau page says the tower is 45.9 feet tall and was built in 1868; the record's 13.7 m (about 45 feet) is close; not checked further. The Forest Service page (last updated 8 Oct 2026) and the Munising page were read 2026-10-27. The Munising snippet's 'privately owned and not open to the public' is in search results only; the story uses the Forest Service and LighthouseFriends for that point. The record's coordinates (46.45666, -86.6232) are within about 0.7 km of the archive's position (46 27.01 N, 86 37.34 W). Do not confuse with the Grand Island North Light (1856), a separate station. The corpus lhb 1899 and 1900 items are cited by scan page; the printed pages were not confirmed (the 1900 index gives printed page 166 for Grand Island Harbor). No newspaper pages were read for this station: Chronicling America searches for the 1903 Manhattan and 1908 range lights turned up nothing usable. Fact-check 2026-10-27 (independent pass): quote check found all 68 quotes on the first run. Checked the sentences against LighthouseFriends, the USLHS roster (six principal keepers, no assistants or women keepers), the Forest Service and Munising pages, and the Board reports (1892 report, scan p. 545, lightning on 5 August 1891; 1899 report, scan p. 221; 1900 report, scan p. 198, crib work completed December 1899). Changed: metres added to feet (252-foot, 200 feet, the 8 by 24 foot crib, the 45 foot crib); 'seemed about to pitch' replaced with the family's fear in LighthouseFriends' words. The 1899 Board report puts the second crib to the west of the house; LighthouseFriends mentions the crib to the east, which the 1899 entry also records as a separate crib. Both are consistent with the Board's text. Still single-source (LighthouseFriends): the 1903 Manhattan details, the 1905-1907 range-light requests, the nine-person rescue, the restoration dates, and the 1913 sale to the Moose Lodge.
